title: Add like fractions with sum greater than one whole
concept: Add fractions with the same denominator, recognize when the sum is greater than one whole, and convert the result when mixed-number form is required.
prerequisites: Add like fractions within one whole
Convert improper fractions to mixed numbers
templateTypes: Add two like fractions where the numerator sum is greater than the denominator
Convert an improper sum into a mixed number
Choose the correct mixed-number answer from close distractors
Explain how many wholes and remaining parts are in the sum
remediationNotes: Use a visual or unit-part model to show that the denominator names the size of each part. Add only the counts of parts, then group denominator-sized sets into wholes.
recheckTemplates: Add two like fractions with a different denominator and write the answer as a mixed number in simplest form.
Show how the improper numerator was regrouped into wholes and leftover parts.
parentTutorNotes: The student is learning that fractions can add to more than one whole. Ask them to count the parts first, then regroup those parts into wholes.
difficultyProgression: Sum is just over one whole and already in simplest form
Sum requires mixed-number conversion
Sum requires mixed-number conversion and simplification
Student explains the regrouping process in words

title: Add unlike fractions using common denominators
concept: Rewrite unlike fractions as equivalent fractions with a shared denominator, then add and simplify the result.
prerequisites: Convert improper fractions to mixed numbers
templateTypes: Add two proper fractions with unlike denominators
Fill missing equivalent-fraction numerators before adding
Add unlike fractions where the sum is greater than one
Choose a common denominator before solving
remediationNotes: Make the same-sized-parts idea explicit. Rewrite both fractions with the same denominator, check each equivalent fraction, then add only the numerators.
recheckTemplates: Add two unlike fractions with denominators that have a manageable common multiple.
Show equivalent-fraction setup and final simplest form.
parentTutorNotes: The student is making the parts the same size before adding. Ask them to show how each fraction changed into an equivalent fraction.
difficultyProgression: One denominator is a multiple of the other
Denominators need a shared multiple that is not one of the originals
Sum requires simplification
Sum requires conversion to mixed-number form

title: Subtract unlike fractions using common denominators
concept: Rewrite unlike fractions with a shared denominator, subtract the numerators, and simplify the difference.
templateTypes: Subtract two unlike proper fractions
Complete missing equivalent-fraction values and subtract
Choose the correct subtraction result from distractors
Explain why a common denominator is needed
remediationNotes: Use a same-sized-parts model. Rewrite both fractions with the same denominator before subtracting counts of parts.
recheckTemplates: Subtract unlike fractions and write both equivalent fractions before subtracting.
parentTutorNotes: Subtraction also needs equal-sized parts. The student should not subtract until both denominators match.
difficultyProgression: One denominator is a multiple of the other
Denominators require a new shared multiple
Result needs simplification
Problem includes distractors that tempt addition or denominator subtraction

title: Subtract a fraction from a whole number
concept: Rename a whole number as denominator-sized parts, subtract the fraction, and express the remaining amount correctly.
prerequisites: Convert whole numbers to equivalent fractions
Convert improper fractions and mixed numbers
templateTypes: Subtract a proper fraction from one whole
Subtract a proper fraction from a whole number greater than one
Rename one whole inside a mixed amount and subtract
Explain why a whole can be written using the fraction denominator
remediationNotes: Rename the whole as a full set of denominator-sized parts. Subtract from that full set, then restore any untouched wholes.
recheckTemplates: Subtract a fraction from a whole number with a different denominator.
Show the whole number as an equivalent fraction before subtracting.
parentTutorNotes: The student is rewriting the whole in matching parts, not changing its value.
difficultyProgression: Subtract from one whole
Subtract from a whole number greater than one
Subtract from a mixed number requiring regrouping
Solve a word problem where a whole item is partly used

title: Add three or more fractions
concept: Add multiple fractions by converting all terms into compatible form, then simplify or convert the final total.
prerequisites: Convert improper fractions to mixed numbers
templateTypes: Add three fractions where two denominators already match
Add three unlike fractions using a shared denominator
Identify efficient grouping before adding
Add multiple fractions where the final result must be simplified or converted
remediationNotes: List every denominator and choose a denominator that works for all terms. Use a checklist to confirm each fraction was converted before addition.
recheckTemplates: Add three fractions with at least two unlike denominators.
Show common-denominator setup for every fraction and write the final simplest-form answer.
parentTutorNotes: This skill checks organization as much as calculation. Encourage the student to account for every fraction before adding.
difficultyProgression: Three fractions where two denominators match
Three fractions where one denominator is a multiple of the others
Three fractions requiring a new shared denominator
Final answer requires simplification and mixed-number conversion

title: Solve addition fraction word problems
concept: Identify joining or combining contexts, add relevant fractional quantities, and report the answer with correct units.
prerequisites: Use bar models or part-whole diagrams
templateTypes: Combine two measured amounts from a shared context
Find total distance, mass, volume, or time from two fractional parts
Use a bar model to represent two known parts being joined
Choose the correct operation before calculating
remediationNotes: Underline the quantities, circle the unit, and draw a parts-joining bar. Add only after the story structure is clear.
recheckTemplates: Solve a joining-context word problem with unlike denominators.
State the operation, show the addition, and include the unit in the answer.
parentTutorNotes: The student should decide the story structure before calculating. Ask whether parts are being combined, compared, or taken away.
difficultyProgression: Two like-denominator quantities in the same unit
Two unlike-denominator quantities in the same unit
Addition result greater than one whole
Context includes extra text or a tempting subtraction phrase

title: Solve subtraction fraction word problems
concept: Identify take-away, difference, or remaining-amount contexts and subtract fractional quantities accurately.
prerequisites: Subtract a fraction from a whole number
Represent part-whole relationships with a bar model
templateTypes: Find how much is left after fractional amounts are used
Find the difference between two measured fractional quantities
Use a total-minus-known-parts structure
Complete a bar model where the unknown is the remaining part
remediationNotes: Identify the starting amount, removed amount, and unknown remainder or difference. Use a bar model to show which segment is missing.
recheckTemplates: Solve a remaining-amount problem where a whole or mixed amount loses a fractional part.
Show operation choice, denominator work, and unit label.
parentTutorNotes: For subtraction stories, find the starting amount and what is being removed or compared before solving.
difficultyProgression: Take away a like-denominator fraction
Take away an unlike-denominator fraction
Subtract from one whole or a mixed number
Use a bar model with total and multiple known parts

title: Solve two-step addition/subtraction fraction word problems
concept: Plan and solve two-step fraction contexts involving addition, subtraction, or working backward.
templateTypes: Add two known parts, then subtract from a total
Work backward from a final amount after one addition and one subtraction event
Find a missing part in a multi-segment bar model
Solve a context where one step uses unlike-denominator addition and the next uses subtraction
remediationNotes: Use a plan-before-calculate routine: identify what is known, what is unknown, and what must be found first. Label Step 1 and Step 2 before arithmetic.
recheckTemplates: Solve a two-step context with one addition step and one subtraction step.
Provide a labeled plan, two operations, and a final answer with units.
parentTutorNotes: This skill is about mathematical planning. The student may know the arithmetic but need help deciding what to find first.
difficultyProgression: Add two known fractions, then subtract from one whole
Subtract one fraction, then add another
Work backward from a final mixed amount
Interpret a multi-segment bar model with an unknown part
